newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: ZKB says Roche price rise excessive.
newsitem.headline: ZKB says Roche price rise excessive.

text.p: Zurich Kantonalbank (ZKB), Switzerland's fourth largest bank, said Wednesday's rise in the shares of Roche Holding AG had more than discounted any possible sale of its fragrances and flavours division and the bank was a seller rather than a buyer of Roche at this level.
In its Daily Market Opinion, ZKB's brokerage research said rumours on Wednesday that Roche would sell its fragrances division had helped boost Roche's non-voting equity securities.
ZKB noted the fragrances and flavours division accounted for 8.9 percent of Roche's sales, but the division's profitability was below the company's average.
Comparing Roche's fragrances division with its main competitor, ZKB estimated that Roche's division would have a market value of around 2.4 billion Swiss francs.
A sale of the division would not only result in a book profit for Roche, but also a higher profitability for the entire group, ZKB said.
"But yesterday's rise in the share price has by far overcompensated for such a move. We would rather be sellers at this level," ZKB's analysts wrote.
On Wednesday Roche's non-voting equity securities rose seven percent to 11,935 francs and continued to rise this morning, hitting a high of 12,160.
Later the securities eased and were five francs higher at 1045 GMT.
